Every registered protocol literal in protocol_registry.py is still '/1'; there is no second major version and no stream-naming code keyed on protocol major version to test rejection/isolation against yet.
Dual-publish-across-versions has no implementation to test; it presumes the new-major-protocol stream-naming work above exists first.

This is an operational rollout runbook (deploy canaries, run synthetic tests, widen the cohort, drain old workers, destroy idle capacity) rather than a single assertable outcome. The individual technical guarantees it leans on -- claim isolation, worker-loss handling -- are unit-tested elsewhere (linked); the sequencing itself is a rehearsed operator procedure, not something this test suite can execute end to end.
There is no versioned controller API (no HTTP transport for claim/launch/result/liveness endpoints yet) and therefore no minor-version-overlap-window logic to test.

No 'migration journal' concept exists in the codebase (confirmed by grep); migrations that would require a filesystem rewrite or table rebuild under a verified backup are not yet distinguished from ordinary transactional migrations.
